reasons: Directionally correct: the edit converts the bare 'are the property of Company' statement into an express, irrevocable assignment of all right, title and interest (including IP) in the Works to us, which is the playbook's preferred position, and it preserves the parties' existing payment-gating (now tightened to the undisputed amount of the relevant invoice) rather than expanding our obligations.

The added subsection covers the two remaining gaps the rule requires: Customer Data ownership and an express no-joint-ownership statement, and it carves Company Data / our pre-existing IP out of 'Contractor's Information' so it cannot be swept into Contractor's exclusive property under 4(b).

No assignment of our IP or data to Contractor is created or left in place; Contractor's background IP (4(b)) and the embedded-IP licence-back (4(c)) are expressly left intact, consistent with the rule's allowance for the Vendor keeping its platform and tools.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (ratio 0.844) is explained by the necessary replacement of the vague 'to the extent ... invoiced and paid' ownership test with assignment language; the operative subject and the rest of the sentence are retained, so no smaller edit would reach the playbook position.

Comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, concise and in first person plural; it states what changed, the playbook basis, and confirms Contractor's retained rights are unaffected. Minor residual risk to confirm on turn: that the inserted lettering '(e)' does not collide with an existing subsection and that 'Services' is a defined term in this MSA.
